rules.statement: VAT shall apply to supplies of goods and services made for consideration within the territory of a Member State by a taxable person acting as such, to intra-Community acquisitions, and to importation of goods.
A taxable person is any person who independently carries out an economic activity, whatever the purpose or result of that activity.
The place of supply of services to a taxable person (B2B) is the place where that customer has established its business (or fixed establishment receiving the service).
The place of supply of services to a non-taxable person (B2C) is the place where the supplier has established its business.
The place of supply of services rendered to a non-taxable person by an intermediary acting in the name and on behalf of another is the place where the underlying transaction is supplied.

The place of supply of services connected with immovable property (estate agents, experts, architects, on-site supervision, accommodation) is the place where the property is located, for both B2B and B2C.
The place of supply of passenger transport is the place where the transport takes place, proportionate to the distances covered.
The place of supply of admission to cultural, artistic, sporting, scientific, educational, entertainment or similar events to a taxable person is the place where those events actually take place.
The place of supply to a non-taxable person of cultural, artistic, sporting, scientific, educational and entertainment activities is the place where those activities actually take place.
The place of supply of restaurant and catering services is the place where the services are physically carried out (except where supplied on board ships, aircraft or trains, art. 57).
The place of short-term hire of a means of transport is where the vehicle is actually put at the disposal of the customer.

The place of supply of telecommunications, broadcasting and electronically supplied services (TBE) to a non-taxable person is the place where that customer is established, has its permanent address or usually resides.

Certain services (consultancy, advertising, intellectual, financial, hiring of movable property) supplied to a non-taxable person established outside the EU are taxed where that customer is established or resides.
Where goods are not dispatched or transported, the place of supply is the place where the goods are located at the time the supply takes place.
Where goods are dispatched or transported, the place of supply is the place where the goods are located when dispatch or transport to the customer begins.
The chargeable event is the occurrence by which the legal conditions for VAT to become chargeable are fulfilled; chargeability is the moment the tax authority becomes entitled to claim the VAT.
The chargeable event occurs and VAT becomes chargeable when the goods or services are supplied.
Supplies giving rise to successive statements of account or successive payments are regarded as completed on expiry of the periods to which those statements or payments relate.
Where a payment on account is made before the goods or services are supplied, VAT becomes chargeable on receipt of the payment and on the amount received.
Member States may derogate to make VAT chargeable no later than issue of the invoice, no later than receipt of payment, or within a set period when no invoice or a late invoice is issued.
For an intra-Community acquisition VAT becomes chargeable on issue of the invoice, or at the latest on the 15th day of the month following the chargeable event.
The taxable amount is everything constituting consideration obtained by the supplier from the customer or a third party, including subsidies linked to the price.
The taxable amount includes taxes, duties, levies and charges (excluding VAT itself) and incidental expenses such as commission, packing, transport and insurance costs charged to the customer.

The taxable amount excludes price reductions for early payment, discounts and rebates granted to the customer, and amounts received as repayment of expenditure paid in the customer's name and account.
In cases of cancellation, refusal, total or partial non-payment, or price reduction after the supply, the taxable amount shall be reduced accordingly under conditions set by the Member State.
The rate applicable is the rate in force at the time of the chargeable event, subject to the derogations on chargeability.
Each Member State shall apply a single standard rate of VAT to supplies of goods and services.
The standard rate of VAT shall not be lower than 15%.
Member States may apply at most two reduced rates, not lower than 5%, only to supplies of goods and services listed in Annex III.
Member States may apply one reduced rate below 5% and one exemption with deductibility (zero rate) to a limited number of Annex III points.
Member States shall exempt certain activities in the public interest, including hospital and medical care, education, and certain postal, welfare and cultural services.
Member States shall exempt certain financial and insurance transactions, granting of credit, transactions in currency and securities, gambling, and the leasing or letting of immovable property.
Member States shall exempt the importation of goods whose supply is exempt, and the importation of goods declared under a special scheme such as IOSS.
The export of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU is exempt from VAT (with deduction).
The intra-Community supply of goods dispatched or transported to a taxable person in another Member State is exempt from VAT.
The ICS exemption requires that the customer be identified for VAT in a Member State other than that of departure and that the supplier hold a valid VAT identification number for that customer.
The ICS exemption does not apply where the supplier has not submitted, or has incorrectly submitted, the recapitulative statement covering the supply (unless duly justified).
An intra-Community acquisition of goods is the acquisition of the right to dispose of movable property dispatched or transported to the acquirer from another Member State.
The place of an intra-Community acquisition of goods is where dispatch or transport of the goods to the acquirer ends.
An intra-Community acquisition is also taxed in the Member State that issued the VAT number used, unless the acquirer proves the acquisition was taxed at the place of arrival.
Triangulation simplification exempts the intermediary's intra-Community acquisition where the goods move directly to a final customer who accounts for the VAT under reverse charge.
VAT is payable by the taxable person carrying out the taxable supply of goods or services, except where another person is liable under articles 194 to 199b and 202.

Member States may provide that the customer is liable for VAT where the taxable supply is made by a supplier not established in the Member State where the VAT is due (optional domestic reverse charge).
VAT is payable by the taxable customer receiving article-44 services supplied by a taxable person not established in the customer's Member State (general B2B cross-border reverse charge).
VAT is payable by the person to whom goods are supplied under a triangular transaction where the conditions of article 141 are met and a compliant invoice is issued.
Member States may apply the reverse charge to designated supplies including construction work, supply of staff, immovable property, used material and scrap.
Member States may apply the reverse charge to fraud-sensitive supplies such as emission allowances, mobile phones, integrated-circuit devices, gas and electricity.
Where the customer is liable for the VAT, the invoice shall carry the words 'Reverse charge' (Reverse charge).
Where a supply is exempt, the invoice shall include a reference to the applicable provision (e.g. 'intra-Community supply, art. 138') or other indication that the supply is exempt.

A taxable person identified for VAT shall submit a recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) listing customers to whom it has made exempt intra-Community supplies of goods and article-44 reverse-charge services.
The recapitulative statement shall in principle be drawn up for each calendar month and submitted within a period not exceeding one month.
The recapitulative statement shall state, per customer VAT identification number, the total value of the goods and services supplied to that customer during the period.
The right of deduction arises at the time the deductible VAT becomes chargeable.
A taxable person may deduct input VAT on goods and services used for the purposes of its taxed transactions.
Member States may operate an optional cash-accounting scheme under which the right of deduction is postponed until the VAT on the supply has been paid to the supplier.
To exercise the right of deduction on a supply of goods or services, the taxable person must hold an invoice drawn up in accordance with the directive's invoicing rules.
Where goods and services are used for both deductible and non-deductible transactions, only the proportion attributable to the deductible transactions (pro rata) is deductible.
The initial deduction shall be adjusted where it was higher or lower than that to which the taxable person was entitled, including a multi-year adjustment period for capital goods.
Every taxable person shall submit a VAT return setting out all the information needed to calculate the VAT chargeable and the deductions to be made.
The VAT return shall be submitted by a deadline set by Member States, no later than two months after the end of each tax period (not exceeding one year).
Member States shall identify by means of an individual VAT number every taxable person making taxable supplies, intra-Community acquisitions, or article-44/196 cross-border services.
A taxable person shall ensure that an invoice is issued for supplies of goods or services made to another taxable person or non-taxable legal person.
For exempt intra-Community supplies of goods and article-196 reverse-charge services, the invoice shall be issued no later than the 15th day of the month following the chargeable event.
A customer's VAT identification number used for an exempt intra-Community supply should be verified as valid and active via the VIES system at the time of supply.
The scope of services 'connected with immovable property' for article 47 is defined by the VAT Implementing Regulation, requiring a sufficiently direct connection with a specific property (verify).

rules.source: VAT Directive art. 73 / national rounding rules (verify)
rules.statement: VAT amounts may be rounded per line or per invoice total according to the consistently applied national rounding convention; rounding must not systematically benefit the taxable person (verify).
Member States may exempt small enterprises whose annual turnover is below a national threshold, with a cross-border SME scheme available up to a Union turnover of EUR 100 000.
Travel agents acting in their own name towards travellers apply the special margin scheme, taxing only the travel agent's margin and with no input-VAT deduction on bought-in travel services.
The margin scheme covers second-hand goods, works of art, collectors' items and antiques supplied by a taxable dealer, as defined in article 311.
Under the margin scheme the taxable amount is the profit margin (selling price less purchase price) less the VAT relating to the margin.
A dealer using the margin scheme may not deduct input VAT on the margin-scheme goods and may not show the VAT separately on the invoice.
The Union One Stop Shop lets a supplier declare and pay, via a single registration, the VAT on intra-EU B2C distance sales of goods and cross-border B2C services in all Member States of consumption.

Cross-border B2C distance sales of goods and TBE services are taxed in the Member State of the supplier until the EUR 10 000 EU-wide annual threshold is exceeded, after which they are taxed in the Member State of consumption.
The non-Union One Stop Shop lets a supplier not established in the EU declare and pay, via a single registration, the VAT on all B2C services supplied to EU consumers.

The Import One Stop Shop allows VAT on distance sales of imported goods in consignments of an intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 (excluding goods subject to excise duty) to be charged at the point of sale and declared via a single registration.
The VAT exemption for imported consignments of negligible value (formerly up to EUR 22) has been abolished, so all commercial imports are subject to VAT regardless of value.
OSS returns are submitted quarterly (Union and non-Union schemes) and IOSS returns monthly, each listing the VAT due per Member State of consumption.

An electronic interface facilitating distance sales of imported goods (consignments up to EUR 150) or certain EU sales by non-EU sellers is deemed to have received and supplied the goods itself and is liable for the VAT.
Under OSS and IOSS the VAT rate applied is the rate of the Member State of consumption (the customer's location).

rules.source: VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) Directive (EU) 2025/516 (verify)
rules.statement: Under the ViDA package, intra-EU B2B transactions will require near-real-time digital reporting based on structured e-invoices, progressively replacing recapitulative statements (verify effective date).
The intra-Community acquisition of goods for consideration by a taxable person acting as such is subject to VAT in the Member State of arrival, accounted for by the acquirer.
On each transaction VAT is chargeable on the price after deduction of the VAT borne directly by the cost components, ensuring the tax is exactly proportional to the price.
